guard_streams.source: Money saving tips for phone, broadband and pay-TV

facts.detail: Ofcom published the money-saving tips guide on 1 July 2026.
The guide advises customers to check whether they remain in a 12, 18 or 24-month minimum contract before switching.
Out-of-contract customers are advised to compare offers and ask their existing provider to match or beat a better deal.
Bundling broadband with landline or pay-TV may reduce cost, although it can reduce flexibility.
The guide recommends checking data, speed and subscription use so customers do not pay for more than they need.

guard_streams.source: Use an Ofcom-accredited price comparison site to find the best deal

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated its accredited price-comparison guide on 17 July 2026.
The guide covers comparison of phone, broadband and pay-TV products.
Accredited services must pass an audit of accessibility, accuracy, transparency, comprehensiveness and freshness.
Ofcom lists accredited services covering combined broadband/mobile/landline/pay-TV, broadband-focused and mobile-focused comparisons.
The guide links customers to Ofcom coverage checking, social tariffs and provider-performance information.

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated its mobile-roaming guide on 6 July 2026.
Mobile providers must publish roaming charges on their websites.
Providers must normally send an automatic message explaining roaming charges or usage limits when a customer enters another country.
Customers can set a monthly spend limit and must be notified when it is likely to be reached.
The guide recommends using Wi-Fi and downloading content before travel to reduce mobile-data charges.

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the mobile-switching guide on 1 July 2026.
Customers can text INFO to 85075 to check contract status and possible early termination charges.
Customers who want to keep their number can text PAC to 65075.
Customers who want a new number can text STAC to 75075.
The provider must return the code within one minute, and the new provider must complete the switch within one working day.

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the landline-switching guide on 1 July 2026.
Under One Touch Switch, the customer contacts the new provider and that provider arranges the switch.
Customers using One Touch Switch are told about applicable early termination charges.
The new provider needs the address, current provider, services to switch and whether the customer wants to keep the phone number.
Customers may need to manage additional bundled services such as pay-TV separately.
